findings.problem: Both soundness theorems contain the same argument. It transfers the table-level facts `quotGt n (genTabs n E) b ≠ idTab n` and `powTab n (quotGt …) p = idTab n` to the group element `quotElt E b`. This uses `quotGt_eq`, `tab_one_toArray`, `tab_pow` and `eq_of_tabArr_eq` with the faithful-base hypothesis. It then supplies a `Fact p.Prime` instance and applies `orderOf_eq_prime`. wit3_sound_of does this at lines 112–122 with p = 3. witP_sound_of does it at lines 173–184 with general p. The two copies differ only in the exponent, and each is about ten lines of non-routine reasoning. A change to the table representation would need two edits.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to quotGt_eq / quotGi_eq in namespace Vol2Native.L239:

theorem orderOf_quotElt_eq_prime {B : List ℕ} (hB : ∀ b ∈ B, b < n) (hbase : ∀ g : Γ, (∀ b ∈ B, act n g b = b) → g = 1) (E : List Γ) {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) {b : QuotGen} (hwb : ∀ l ∈ b.w, l < E.length) (hne : quotGt n (genTabs n E) b ≠ idTab n) (hpow : powTab n (quotGt n (genTabs n E) b) p = idTab n) : orderOf (quotElt E b) = p

Proof sketch: set hTb := quotGt_eq (n := n) E b hwb. Show quotElt E b ≠ 1 by `intro h1; apply hne; rw [hTb, h1, tab_one_toArray]`. Show quotElt E b ^ p = 1 by `eq_of_tabArr_eq hB hbase` followed by `rw [tab_pow, tab_one_toArray, ← hTb]; exact hpow`. Finish with `haveI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩; exact orderOf_eq_prime _ _`.

In wit3_sound_of, delete hb1', hb3' and hord (lines 113–122, keeping hTb only if hcomm still needs it). Replace them with `have hord : orderOf (quotElt E b) = 3 := orderOf_quotElt_eq_prime hB hbase E Nat.prime_three hwb hb1 hb3`. The hypotheses hb1 and hb3 come from the Wit3Ok destructuring.

In witP_sound_of, delete hb1', hbp', the Fact line and hord (lines 175–184). Replace them with `have hord : orderOf (quotElt E b) = p := orderOf_quotElt_eq_prime hB hbase E hp hwb hb1 hbp`. The hypotheses hb1 and hbp come from the WitPOk destructuring.
findings.benefit: The "table says order p ⇒ group element has order p" step lives in one named, separately tested lemma. Each soundness theorem then reads as a short mathematical argument instead of re-deriving the table-to-group transfer. Changes to quotGt/quotElt or to the faithful-action hypothesis are made in one place.
